content: Binding to 127.0.0.1/localhost is NOT sufficient protection: DNS rebinding lets an attacker-controlled webpage's DNS entry resolve to 127.0.0.1 after the browser's same-origin check, so any site the user visits in another tab can send requests to the loopback server. Real-world precedent: Vite's dev server had no Host-header validation, patched Jan 2025 (GHSA-vg6x-rcgg-rjx6) after being show exploitable; webpack-dev-server and Parcel had the same class of bug. The fix is to validate the Host header against an explicit allowlist (localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1] + configured port) on every request, reject non-loopback Origin on CORS and WebSocket upgrade, and never send wildcard Access-Control-Allow-Origin. A browser cannot forge the Host header, so Host validation defeats DNS rebinding even though CORS alone does not.
